title: How are student NGOs funded without donations? · AquaTerra
description: How AquaTerra pays for welfare work without donations: Paradox, Disco Diwali, The Starry Night and fundraiser matches. {count} nights and drives since {firstYear}.
lede: AquaTerra takes no monetary donations and charges no fees, so its welfare drives are paid for by its own student-run events. The main ones are Paradox, Disco Diwali, TerraThon, The Starry Night and fundraiser matches, along with the streetwear label Crftd. This page gathers {count} of the nights and drives behind that work, from {firstYear} to {lastYear}.

sections.heading: no donations, no fees
body: AquaTerra takes no monetary donations and charges no fees. That leaves the welfare work to be paid for another way, and the way AquaTerra does it is through its own student-run events. The work is self-funded, and the nights are how it is done.

Crftd, AquaTerra's student streetwear label, was called ROOTS at first. Its tees turned up on school days in July and August 2025, when students at four schools wore them on Morpheus, Concord, Confluence and Novus days.

sections.heading: the nights that pay for the work
body: Paradox is the multi-day fest. It began in January 2022 as an online mini fete, Paradox 1.0, and its third edition in June 2025 ran for five days with twelve events, a Punjabi Night and around three hundred volunteers.

Disco Diwali started at New Alipore in October 2024, and its second edition ran in October 2025 at Chowringhee Banquets, with a photo booth, masks and a silver-tinsel dance floor. The Starry Night, a winter carnival at Sky Turf, ran in December 2024 and December 2025. Fundraiser matches at VS Arena, Elgin Turf and Hindustan Road covered football, basketball and FIFA gaming.

sections.heading: what a night looks like
body: A night is a team job. Starry Night '25 at Sky Turf brought hundreds of people together for music and giving back, and the basketball fundraiser Shoot for the Stars at Chetla Park Athletic Club in December 2024 had thirty volunteers running matches, stalls and merchandise.

The sporting nights show the range. Turf Wars was a football fundraiser at Elgin Turf in March 2022, Inception '22 was a basketball tournament in June 2022, and the FIFA fundraiser in May 2023 ran over two days at Hindustan Road, with gaming prizes and a cause to play for.

sections.heading: how to take part
body: Students can take part by coming to a night, joining the team that runs one, or writing up the day afterwards. Each night is written up with its name, edition, date and place, so the work is public.

Companies can take part too, though AquaTerra does not ask for donations. A company can sponsor one of the nights, have a stall at a fundraising night, or work with the team on a drive. Start with the [collaborations page](/collaborations) or the [contact page](/contact).

learnings: Student-run nights are how the welfare work is paid for, because AquaTerra takes no donations and charges no fees.
A night can be a sports tournament, a dance night or a carnival, so it follows what students are good at.
A streetwear label and a set of nights can both pay for the same welfare work, so the money does not rest on one event.
Each night is written up with its date and place, so anyone can see what the work was.

faqs.q: How do student NGOs pay for their work without donations?
faqs.a: AquaTerra, a student NGO in Kolkata, pays for its welfare drives through its own student-run events, including Paradox, Disco Diwali, TerraThon, The Starry Night and fundraiser matches, plus the streetwear label Crftd. It takes no monetary donations and charges no fees.
No. AquaTerra takes no monetary donations. Companies can take part by sponsoring one of the fundraising nights, having a stall at one, or working with the team on a drive.

faqs.q: What events does AquaTerra run to fund its work?
faqs.a: Paradox, a multi-day fest in June 2025 with twelve events, Disco Diwali in October 2024 and October 2025 and in November 2026, The Starry Night in December 2024 and December 2025, and TerraThon, a student sports festival held from 2 to 4 October 2026.
Yes. AquaTerra takes no donations and charges no fees, so its welfare drives are paid for by its own student-run events and by Crftd.
Crftd is AquaTerra's student streetwear label, and it was called ROOTS at first. Its tees were worn on school days in July and August 2025, and it helps pay for AquaTerra's welfare work.
